sourceEdition: OUR/IM 2017–2019 CC BY 4.0 lineage; separate photo/graphic attributions preserved at publisher site
method: Read public complete student activity text and public teacher lesson narrative/activities plus preparation learning goals, not protected teacher model responses; compare to Grade 6 first-party candidate and add differentiated original numerical/source-adjacent examples.

lessons.title: More about Constant Speed
sourceTasks: Two walkers 24 miles apart approach at 3 and 3.4 miles per hour; tabulate separation and meeting clock time
Change one walker's speed for a later 2.5-hour meeting; interpret relative closing speed
Dog moving between walkers, different starting speeds, and opposite-direction swim/bike challenge
representationAndAssessmentRequirements: distance-gap table with labeled time and miles
opposing-direction motion visual or teacher-reviewed original diagram
recognition that path distance and displacement differ
firstPartyOriginalTeachingAdded: Four-state separation table and 11:45 a.m. meeting
Exact 6.2-mph changed running rate and 22.5-mile dog path under explicit assumptions
Treadmill pace/speed and opposite direction 3.125-mile separation examples

criteria: Model closing vs separating rates correctly
Present a labeled table and justify the reasoning

caveats: No original rail-trail photo copied; students' physical representations not collected.

lessons.title: Solving Rate Problems
sourceTasks: Flash three differently shaded 10-by-10 hundred grids and describe fraction/decimal shading
Use unavailable original offer cards in partner critique/sort and invent a persuasive deal
Compare six fictional animal distances in yards, miles, inches, meters, kilometers and feet by converting to common meters
Select units and justify mathematical interpretation rather than only a number
representationAndAssessmentRequirements: tactile or accessible textual hundred-square representation
real original publisher offer cards are a separate media/pedagogical dependency
source unit conversion table with explicit precision and ranking
teacher-scored cooperative evidence and oral explanation
firstPartyOriginalTeachingAdded: Six fictional distance conversions with 1.04-centimeter coyote/ostrich difference
First-party offer scenario clearly distinguished from unverified source A–F cards

criteria: Give a justified grid decomposition rather than unsupported shading number
Convert all fictional sprint distances to one unit before ranking
Human-score partner discussion and self-created offers with units

caveats: Original card set A–F not authenticated or copied; do not claim equivalent delivery.
Original figures absent: text description does not prove visual accessible renderer.

lessons.title: What Are Percentages?
sourceTasks: Mentally convert cents and dollars in both directions
Match six commonly denominated US coin amounts to percentages of one dollar
Reason about six dimes and six quarters relative to the dollar baseline
Describe two disjoint coin-type combinations at 120% of $1
Use original or equivalent double number line for coin amounts from 0 through 150%
representationAndAssessmentRequirements: money-versus-percent double number line with labeled aligned marks
coin drawings are source-specific graphics and not verified in product
comparison percent may be greater than 100
open coin-combination task requires checking distinct types
firstPartyOriginalTeachingAdded: First-party coin table with denomination and value/per-100 rates
Six dimes 60%, six quarters 150%, and three quarters/five dimes 125%
Two alternative 120-cent sets with disjoint coin types

criteria: Explain why 150 cents is 150% rather than invalid

caveats: United States Mint coin artwork is not copied or licensed through Edulytiks by this update.

lessons.title: Percentages and Double Number Lines
sourceTasks: Compare three fundraising achievements to one $40 reference at 50%, 100%, 150%
Map 75%, 100% and 125% to an 8-mile biking reference with a double number line
Infer different predicted adult puppy weights when 9 pounds denotes 20% versus 30% of adult reference
Optional historical relative price and wage percentage as a stipulated algebraic comparison
representationAndAssessmentRequirements: aligned percent-distance double number line with equal interval spacing
inverse percentage use: part known, reference whole unknown
above-100% comparisons not treated as impossible
open student explanation evaluated by teacher
firstPartyOriginalTeachingAdded: Complete percent-mile line with 25% increments from 0 to 150%
9-lb puppy part at 20% gives 45-lb reference versus 30% gives 30-lb reference
Historical 0.20/2.50=8% illustrative comparison not a verified inflation figure

criteria: Solve part-of-whole and inverse whole problems with correct operation
Keep diagram marks and corresponding units accessible
Explain estimates and avoid real health/economic claims

caveats: No teacher-confirmed authenticated visuals or puppy responses.
Historical bread and wage figures are classroom data only, not present-day facts.
